title: optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization, pin thread pools, and improve scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers reported tail latency variance on small-text workloads where CPU-side work (serialization, request routing, and thread pool contention) dominated wall-clock time. This PR targets CPU-side bottlenecks in the serving request path: reduce serialization overhead for internal RPCs, pin worker thread pools to CPU cores on host environments where pinning is allowed, and introduce a lightweight scheduling pass to reduce head-of-line contention in the batching/scheduling layer. Summary of changes: 1) Replace JSON-based internal request marshaling in hot-path with a compact binary envelope (tiny header + flatbuffer-style payload) for in-process and unix-socket RPCs; reduces per-request allocate/parse cost. 2) Introduce RequestContext pooling to reuse pre-allocated scratch buffers (KV cache headers, token buffers) across short-lived requests. 3) Add a new pinned_worker_pool with optional cpu-affinity config; on Linux systems with cpuset permissions the pool pins threads to adjacent cores to reduce cache thrashing. 4) Scheduling improvement: lightweight cooperative scheduling on the batcher that avoids waking all workers for small jobs and favors workers with warm KV cache. 5) Metrics and tracing: per-request CPU-time and serialization-time metrics, and a new diagnostic trace tag (cpu.pin-group) to track affinity groups during experiments. 6) Config and rollout: feature guarded behind runtime flags (enable_cpu_optimizations) and a per-cluster opt-in via configmap for Dedicated/Private deployments. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on c5.4xlarge-like instance with a 512-token average workload show p50 latency improvement of ~18% and p95 improvement of ~12% for CPU-dominated request mix; end-to-end throughput improved ~9% under contention. In our internal perf canary (perf-canary/redwood) we saw 6% lower CPU utilization for the same QPS for inference paths that hit shared KV cache. Risk and mitigation: affinity pinning can worsen colocated noisy-neighbor interference on multi-tenant hosts; we default to disabled in hosted and enable only for Dedicated/Private clusters where customers control placement. Feature gated and rollout via canary followed by staged cluster opt-ins. Tests: adds unit tests for RequestContext pooling, affinity toggle, and new serialization parity tests; adds stress test in perf-canary harness to validate throughput under high concurrency. Related: builds on previous batching/kv-cache work (ENG-4310) and is part of perf epic ENG-4521. See inline docs in runtime/README-CPU-OPT.md for operational guidance and flags.
